findings.evidence: Line 323-324 makes the claim; grep of the file shows no `One`/`trivial`/`IsPureGauge` declaration, only `MulAction (V → G) (GaugeLink V G)` at line 145. The claim is provable: for symmetric `B`, `bilinPhase B x y = (B x x - B y y)/2`, so `ofBilin B x y = Ω x * 1 * (Ω y)⁻¹` with `Ω x = Circle.exp (B x x / 2)`, matching `smul_apply` (line 140).
findings.fix: Add `instance : One (GaugeLink V G) := ⟨fun _ _ => 1, …⟩` with a `@[simp] one_apply`, and the lemma `B.flip = B → ofBilin B = (fun x => Circle.exp (B x x / 2)) • 1` (and/or the corollary that the staple link equals the straight link when `B` is symmetric, from `pathLink_staplePath_ofBilin` with `B - B.flip = 0`); otherwise delete the claim from the docstring.
findings.issue: The `ofBilin` docstring asserts "when `B` is symmetric the potential is a pure gauge", but the API cannot express or prove it: there is no trivial gauge link (no `One (GaugeLink V G)`, no `GaugeLink.trivial`) for the `MulAction (V → G)` introduced at line 145 to act on, so no consumer can state that a link is a pure gauge or compare a link to the trivial one.

findings.evidence: Lines 335-336 have no attribute; `EpsilonEridani/QFT/SmallX/Dipole/WilsonLine.lean:78` `@[simp] gaugeTransform_apply` and `:106` `@[simp] adjointLine_apply` are the repo pattern. The file's own proofs need `rw [... ofBilin_apply ...]`/`simp [ofBilin_apply, hB]` (lines 343, 370).
findings.fix: Mark `ofBilin_apply` `@[simp]`, and `transverseLink_smul` and `pathLink_staplePath_smul` `@[simp]` as well (none loops: each pushes `Ω` outward or replaces `ofBilin` by `Circle.exp`). Leave `pathLink_smul` unannotated because of its dependent `getLast` argument.
findings.issue: `ofBilin_apply` is the only computation rule for `ofBilin` (its body is unexposed and uses the `private bilinPhase`), yet it is not `@[simp]`, unlike the analogous `*_apply` rules elsewhere in the repo. Same gap for the gauge-covariance normal forms `transverseLink_smul` (line 254) and `pathLink_staplePath_smul` (line 261), while the link-level `smul_apply` (line 139) is `@[simp]`, so `(Ω • W).transverseLink …` and `(Ω • W).pathLink (staplePath …)` stay stuck for `simp`.

findings.evidence: Lines 221-236: `omit [Module ℝ V] in` before each of the three declarations, and `def staplePath (v w x y : V) : List V := [x, x + v, x + v + w, y]` takes no `GaugeLink` argument, in contrast to `transverseLink (W : GaugeLink V G) …` at line 241.
findings.fix: Move `staplePath`, `staplePath_def` and `reverse_staplePath` out of `namespace GaugeLink` into the enclosing `TMD` namespace (`TMD.staplePath`), updating the references in `pathLink_staplePath`, `pathLink_staplePath_smul`, `pathLink_reverse_staplePath`, `pathLink_staplePath_of_legs_eq_one`, `pathLink_staplePath_of_isAxialGauge`, `pathLink_staplePath_ofBilin`, `exists_isAxialGauge_pathLink_staplePath_ne_one` and the module docstring entry at line 62.
findings.issue: `staplePath`, `staplePath_def` and `reverse_staplePath` are exported in the `GaugeLink` namespace but mention no gauge link at all — they are list-of-corners constructions in an `AddCommGroup` (each is preceded by `omit [Module ℝ V] in`). Dot notation `W.staplePath` cannot resolve, so the namespace misdescribes the object users must spell as `GaugeLink.staplePath`.

summary: The core interface (GaugeLink with FunLike/@[ext], pathLink with its nil/singleton/cons_cons simp lemmas, (rfl)-style *_def restatements so no body is exposed) is sound and carries no free data. Three surface defects: an unstatable docstring claim about pure gauge (no trivial link exists), a missing @[simp] on the only computation rule for ofBilin, and gauge-link-independent declarations sitting in the GaugeLink namespace.
